english_verification.review_scope: Representative opening history and flavour/name checks, bounded Wiki reading for origin, predecessor and setting context; no exhaustive mission audit, playtest or new Reddit/map fetch. Native English idea names/descriptions were compared by localisation key with the current Mod. Wide line ranges locate separately read passages, not exhaustive coverage. No formal validator, build, browser or gameplay test was run.

rationale.campaign_length: The structured catalogue confirms 73 direct B38 missions, with the Entef continuation gated by country flags; no B15-exclusive missions were found.
rationale.colonization: The missions focus on settlement, conquest and state-building in Escann rather than overseas colonisation.
rationale.complexity: Formation gates, optional population policy, conversion, monuments, powerful-mage conditions and later missions run in parallel.
rationale.dark_story: Religious war, an orc-purge branch and an undead army provide the dark side, while another route emphasises protection and construction.
rationale.difficulty: Early competition for land, mid-game resource gates and late powerful-mage conditions may stall progress; no playtest measurement has been performed.
rationale.diplomacy: The foreign settlers need allies early, then contact Kheterata and encourage other countries to adopt Dalcabba.
rationale.early_pressure: B15 competes for land among Escanni adventurers; even with a powerful mage as leader, it must establish a territory quickly.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: A powerful mage leader, mage-priests, magical obelisks, Entef's return and an undead army form the core identity.
rationale.narrative_density: Exile, migration, formation, religious synthesis, population choices, monumental works and the founder's return form a continuous long campaign.
rationale.tall_play: Food, bazaars, a university, pyramids, obelisks and restoration of the old city are all long-term development goals.
rationale.trade_economy: Cotton, gems, bazaars and ties to Kheterata finance large construction projects.
rationale.warfare: Competition among Escanni adventurers, religious war, recovery of the old capital and regional unification span the campaign.

identity.appearance: Start in 1444 as the New Wanderers B15 adventurer company; after meeting the Escanni formation conditions, form Elikhand B38 and switch to its exclusive missions.
identity.formation_scope: B15 must have the Adventurer state-building reform, administrative technology 7 and land in the specified Escanni area; the generic decision uses change_tag = B38 and swap_non_generic_missions, with no fixed formation date.

predecessors.relationship: A Kheteratan exile adventurer company starting in 1444 that forms B38 through the generic Escanni formation decision.

gaps.reason: No unambiguous tag/culture national idea definition found; no predecessor inference.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: Named after our homeland, the Kheteratan Horses are an exceptionally swift breed of horse that we alone use. Unlike the ugly, stocky horses of Escann, our Kheteratans are sleek, nimble and fast as the wind.
description.text_en: Named after our homeland, the Kheteratan Horses are an exceptionally swift breed of horse that we alone use. Unlike the ugly, stocky horses of Escann, our Kheteratans are sleek, nimble and fast as the wind.

description.text: Borrowing from our origins in Kheterata, the architecture of our buildings, from humble dwelling to mighty castle, are constructed with zeal and deep faith. The walls are covered in hieroglyphics and frescoes, and the pillars and obelisks are oriented towards our homeland, Kheterata.

The walls are covered in hieroglyphics and frescoes, and the pillars and obelisks are oriented towards our homeland, Kheterata.

description.text: Our cavalry forces are far superior to the Escanni or other pale peoples, for ours utilize the natural speed of our mounts, while they rely on heavy armor. Called Pursuer Swarms, our cavalry aims to outflank the enemy, and harass them to the point of exhaustion.

description.text: Although it has been many years since the founding of Elikhand, our people still look back and think about their homeland of Kheterata. However, they realize that their lives are now bound to this land, and that our people must be loyal to each other.

description.text: Allowing for decentralized markets along the streets, called bazaars, our nation has become known for easy access for trade goods to be bought and sold.
description.text_en: Allowing for decentralized markets along the streets, called bazaars, our nation has become known for easy access for trade goods to be bought and sold.

description.text: In our homeland of Kheterata, the sickle was a staple weapon of war, but since our arrival in Escann it has lost its place. Facing enemies clad in full-plate armor, weapons were required that could pierce armor. However, now that warfare has shifted to soldiers wielding lighter weight equipment, bladed weapons have once again become useful. Thus, the sickle has once again rightfully found its place in war.

description.text: Escann is a cold land, lacking in the warm sands and constant temperatures of our homeland. Freezing temperatures, although not totally foreign to us, cause vast amounts of "snow" to blanket our lands, causing vast famine. Despite this, we have persevered, and made a home in this land that we call the Land of the Pale Sun.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who want a short mission tree, do not want to wait for major construction and powerful-mage gates, or dislike religious war.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Compete for land and form B38 early; build a New Kheterata, choose a population policy and spread Dalcabba in the middle game; unify Escann, restore the old capital and monuments, and pursue Entef's return late.
player_overview.overview: Start with the Elikhetist New Wanderers adventurer company led by the powerful mage Entef, establish a foothold in Escann and form Elikhand. You must win wars, feed immigrants, build bazaars and monuments, integrate local people and spread Dalcabba. Later you can build pyramids and restore the preserved founder. The choice between accepting and expelling orcs and goblins, religious war and magical rule determines the cost of the ideal homeland.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy Escanni adventurers, religious and cultural synthesis, monuments, powerful mages and long campaigns.
signature_features: The B15 adventurer company forms B38 and switches to 73 direct missions covering a long exile-to-state story.
Agriculture, bazaars, a university and monumental construction run alongside religious conquest.
After meeting the conditions, the founder-mage Entef can return as a mummy and unlock a continuation of magical rule.
player_overview.tagline: Lead exiles to statehood in Escann and turn their new home into a Kheteratan land of magic and monuments.

reasons: A complete epic arc from an exiled adventurer company to a cross-cultural state
Monument building and religious spread run together rather than reducing the campaign to map painting
Entef's mummy continuation gives magical rule a strong narrative identity
warnings: The early game requires competition for land and the formation gates in Escann.
Monument construction and powerful-mage conditions can slow the later campaign.
The orc-purge and religious-exclusion branches differ sharply in values.

positive_indicators: Recognising that residents of different origins should share the new country's prosperity
Building food supplies, bazaars and a university and repairing war-damaged cities
The orc-and-goblin acceptance route improves tolerance and local development; Entef's rescue missions explicitly aim to reduce forced labour.
values.rationale: War, theocracy, conversion and an undead leader are not inherently good or evil. Food, markets, universities, reconstruction and the goal of reducing subjects' forced labour provide substantial public benefits; the acceptance route also recognises orcs and goblins as members of the country. However, the local missions allow expelling or purging orcs for military gains, religious expansion is exclusionary, and undead and mage authority can become concentrated. The two population branches differ greatly, so the overall result is provisionally neutral and branch-dependent; benevolent narration is not treated as a fact about every route.
red_flags: The orc route can trigger expulsion or purging and add genocide-type national actions.
Religious war and broad conversion can reduce the space for dissenting communities.
Entef's return and the magical-elite route concentrate power heavily.
